entry.title: 2027 Equities Mod1-Q1
entry.itemBody: Audrey Lake is the Chief Investment Officer of Mid States University Management Corporation (MSUMC), an endowment fund overseeing the university’s investment portfolio. MSUMC invests over half of its assets in equity securities, both public and private. As part of the equity review process, Lake has assigned the analyst team questions to consider. First, MSUMC’s Investment Office is more interested in being able to benefit from improved company performance than the seniority of claims when they invest. Second, MSUMC’s Investment Office seeks a “voice” in management decisions of the companies in which they invest. Third, MSUMC targets broad exposure across the equity universe, buying both publicly listed and private equities across company life-cycle stages. Finally, MSUMC has a very long investment horizon. Which of the following securities has the lowest seniority on claiming cash flows from a portfolio company?

choices.itemBody: A. Debt
B. Preference shares

C. Common shares Feedback Choice C is correct. Holders of common shares have the residual claim on a company’s cash flows and assets. Common shareholders are paid once all other claims are settled. Choice A is incorrect as debtholders have the highest seniority in receiving cash flows relative to preference and common shareholders. Choice B is incorrect as preference shareholders are senior to common shareholders.

entry.title: 2027 Equities Mod1-Q2
entry.itemBody: Which of the following provides the most correct response as to why MSUMC prefers investing in common shares rather than preference shares?

choices.itemBody: A. Common shares typically provide higher dividends than are received from holding preference shares.
B. Common shares provide the opportunity to vote on corporate decisions in addition to the possibility for improved dividends or higher stock price as company performance improves.

C. Dividends on common shares are less uncertain because of the higher seniority of common shares’ payoffs. Feedback Choice B is correct. MSUMC’s stated goals of being able to capitalize on improvements and having a “voice” on corporate decisions best match the features of common shares. Choice A is incorrect as common shares may have lower or higher dividends than preference shares. Choice C is incorrect as common shares are less senior than preference shares.

entry.title: 2027 Equities Mod1-Q3
entry.itemBody: In which company life-cycle stage is MSUMC most likely to find both publicly listed and private company equities as investments?

choices.itemBody: A. Start-up
B. Growth

C. Mature Feedback Choice C is correct. In the mature stage of the company life cycle, MSUMC is likely to find both publicly listed equity and private equity securities. Publicly listed companies are often mature stage companies, while buyout equity companies in private equity are often mature stage companies. Choice A is incorrect as start-up companies are unlikely to qualify for public listing because of insufficient revenue and profitability. Choice B is incorrect given that growth stage companies may not have achieved the profitability or other characteristics needed for public listing.

entry.title: 2027 Equities Mod1-Q4
entry.itemBody: MSUMC’s long investment horizon is most relevant to which one of the following equity market features in their decision to allocate between publicly listed and private equities?

choices.itemBody: A. Owner–manager separation versus overlap
B. Standardized disclosures versus limited disclosures

C. Liquidity versus illiquidity of shares Feedback Choice C is correct. MSUMC’s long investment horizon allows them to consider holding illiquid private shares if they earn, on average, a higher return than public share holdings. Choice A is incorrect as this feature is more relevant to MSUMC if they want to be able to exert greater management control through equity ownership, and it is independent of MSUMC’s investment horizon. Choice B is incorrect as the disclosure requirements are also independent of MSUMC’s investment horizon.

entry.title: 2027 Equities Mod1-Q5
entry.itemBody: Participating preference shares are least likely to entitle the shareholders to participate in:

choices.itemBody: A. corporate decisions through voting rights.
B. additional distribution of the company’s assets upon liquidation.

C. additional dividends if the company’s profits exceed a predetermined level. Feedback: Correct. Participating preference shares do not entitle the shareholders to participate in corporate decisions through voting rights. But they do entitle them to (1) an additional dividend if the company’s profits exceed a prespecified level and (2) additional distribution of the company’s assets upon liquidation, above the par.

entry.title: 2027 Equities Mod1-Q6
entry.itemBody: A company has issued only one class of common shares, and it does not pay dividends on them. It has also issued two types of non-cumulative preference shares: one that is putable and the other callable. Which of these securities will most likely offer the lowest expected return to the investor?

choices.itemBody: A. Common shares
B. Putable preference shares

C. Callable preference shares Feedback: B is correct. Putable preference shares are less risky than their callable counterparts. They give the investor the option to put the shares back to the company. Because of the lower risk, they will provide a lower expected rate of return. Common shares are the most risky, whether or not they are dividend paying, and are likely to offer the highest expected return.

entry.title: 2027 Equities Mod1-Q7
entry.itemBody: Preference shares are less risky than common shares because preference shares have:

choices.itemBody: A. fixed dividends.
B. a guaranteed return if a company is liquidated.

C. a larger portion of total return based on future price return. Feedback: A correct because dividends on preference shares are known and fixed, and they account for a large portion of the preference shares’ total return. Therefore, there is less uncertainty about future cash flows.

entry.title: 2027 Equities Mod1-Q8
entry.itemBody: Firms with which of the following characteristics are most likely candidates for a management buyout (MBO)?

choices.itemBody: A. Firms with low levels of cash flow
B. Firms with high dividend payout ratios

C. Firms with large amounts of undervalued assets Feedback: C is correct. Companies with large amounts of undervalued assets (which can be sold to reduce debt) that generate high levels of cash flow (which are used to make interest and principal payments on the debt) are likely candidates for MBO transactions
A. are listed on public exchanges.
B. are illiquid and difficult to trade.

C. have easily available financial information. Feedback: B is correct because private equity securities do not have “market determined” quoted prices, are highly illiquid, and require negotiations between investors in order to be traded.
